title: When the Passage Turns
premise: Noor Reyes, a debt-ridden storm chaser who measures life in miles, is handed a dying prospector's map to the source of the Río Sereno in exchange for a promise to carry it home. Racing the expiration of the prospector's concession permits, Noor follows the river upstream with the prospector's estranged grandson, Elian, a cartographer who believes the map is a con. Through floods, sabotage by the concession company's enforcers, and a love neither planned, Noor discovers the prospector was his own grandfather — and that the 'source' is a valley of unregistered land that legally belongs to whoever holds the promise, not the permit. In the climax, Noor chooses love and truth over the money that would clear his debts, filing the promise as inheritance and burning the debt ledger, ending with him and Elian mapping the valley for the people who live there.
about_author: Rosalind Nystrom is a former river guide who spent a decade leading expeditions through remote watersheds before turning to fiction full-time. She writes adventure novels about people whose debts — financial, familial, and moral — pull them into wild places.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Chasing a supercell across the plains to earn hazard pay, Noor counts his debts the way he counts miles. A collector named Voss reminds him the 'optimists' he owes don't forgive. Emotional beat: restless exhaustion, a man outrunning his own life.

chapters.title: The Man Who Sold the Rain
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. In a border-town bar, dying prospector Aurelio Reyes trades Noor a weathered map for a promise: carry it to the source of the Río Sereno before the concession permits expire in ninety days. Noor recognizes the surname but says nothing. Emotional beat: uneasy fascination.

chapters.title: Terms of a Promise
chapters.summary: Elian's POV. Cartographer Elian Reyes, Aurelio's estranged grandson, intercepts Noor, convinced the map is a scam and Noor a con artist preying on a dying man. He insists on coming along. Emotional beat: prickly distrust masking grief.

chapters.title: Ninety Days
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The pair buys a battered river boat and provisions, discovering the permit expiry is real and the concession company, Halcyon Terra, has enforcers on the water. Emotional beat: reluctant partnership forged under a deadline.

chapters.title: First Rapids
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. A violent rapid run nearly capsizes them; Elian's precise navigation saves them, and Noor's storm instincts save Elian in return. First flickers of respect — and attraction. Emotional beat: adrenaline becoming trust.

chapters.title: What the Map Doesn't Show
chapters.summary: Elian's POV. Elian notices the map bears annotations in handwriting identical to letters he received as a child from a grandfather he was told abandoned the family. He confronts Noor, who deflects. Emotional beat: suspicion curdling into hurt.

chapters.title: The Company Man
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss, hired by Halcyon Terra when his debt collection dries up, tracks Noor upstream, realizing the map's valley is unregistered land worth a fortune. Emotional beat: cold ambition rationalized as pragmatism.

chapters.title: River of Small Betrayals
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Supply theft at a trading post forces Noor to admit he's broke and that Voss's collectors are closing in. Elian covers the shortfall with his own savings. Emotional beat: shame met with unexpected grace.

chapters.title: Night of the Flood
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A flash flood traps them in a canyon; sheltering in a cave, soaked and shaking, they stop pretending. The kiss is clumsy, terrified, real. Emotional beat: love arriving like weather.

chapters.title: Letters in the Lining
chapters.summary: Elian's POV. Repairing the map's oilcloth backing, Elian finds letters sewn inside — Aurelio's confession that he had a son he never claimed, Noor's father. He says nothing, watching Noor. Emotional beat: knowledge as a weight.

chapters.title: The Toll Bridge
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Halcyon Terra's enforcers control the last crossing and offer Noor a deal: the map for his debt, cleared. He refuses — and realizes he no longer knows why the promise matters more than money. Emotional beat: identity tipping.

chapters.title: Detour Through Ash Country
chapters.summary: Elian's POV. A burned-out logging region forces a brutal portage. Elian finally reveals what he found in the map's lining. Noor's denial cracks. Emotional beat: betrayal, then the beginning of understanding.

chapters.title: The Son Aurelio Kept
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. A satellite phone call to his mother confirms it: Aurelio was her father-in-law's brother — Noor's grandfather, who chose the river over the family. Noor rages at a dead man and keeps walking upstream. Emotional beat: grief for a stranger who was blood.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Voss's men slash the boat's hull at anchor. Repairs cost them four days; the permit clock now nearly impossible. Noor proposes the reckless shortcut through the gorge. Elian refuses to let him go alone. Emotional beat: fear sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: The Gorge
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The gorge run is a nightmare of whitewater; the boat is destroyed, Elian nearly drowns, and Noor hauls him out half-dead. They continue on foot. Emotional beat: love proven at the edge of loss.

chapters.title: Permit Expiry
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. The permits lapse; Voss is ordered to seize the valley by force before anyone else knows it exists. He hesitates for the first time, watching the two men's firelight from a ridge. Emotional beat: the optimist's ledger developing a conscience.

chapters.title: The Source
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They reach the valley: a hidden basin of springs, terraces, and families who have farmed there for generations without papers. The 'forbidden source' is a community. Emotional beat: awe, then moral clarity.

chapters.title: Whose Land, Whose Name
chapters.summary: Elian's POV. Elian deciphers Aurelio's final annotation: the promise itself is the deed — Aurelio registered the valley under a trust payable to whoever keeps his promise. Noor isn't a courier; he's the heir. Emotional beat: inheritance redefined.

chapters.title: Voss at the Headwaters
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Voss arrives with enforcers to claim the valley for Halcyon Terra. Noor stands between the guns and the farmers and offers Voss the truth: the trust is valid, the seizure is theft. Emotional beat: courage without a weapon.

chapters.title: The Ledger Burns
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Voss defects, handing Noor the company's internal file and burning his own debt ledger in the valley fire. Enforcers stand down as the trust documents go out by satellite uplink. Emotional beat: debts dissolved by choice, not payment.

chapters.title: What We Carry Home
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Weeks later, Noor files Aurelio's promise with the land registry; the valley's families gain legal standing. He and Elian begin mapping the basin together — for them, not for a company. Emotional beat: a promise kept, an identity chosen.

chapters.title: Where the River Begins
chapters.summary: Elian's POV. At the true spring, they bury Aurelio's compass and read his last letter aloud. Noor stops measuring life in miles. The river runs downstream toward everything they left, and they stay at the beginning. Emotional beat: arrival, and a new way of counting time.
